headline: D-Wave has delivered its Advantage2 quantum annealing computer to Como in northern Italy, where it is being installed as the country's first machine of its kind.
score_reason: Company installation announcement with a ceremony still to come; regional significance.
importance_line: It gives Italian and European researchers and companies local access to quantum annealing, a technique suited to optimisation problems, but the usefulness claims come from D-Wave and the system is not yet operating.
summary: The Quantum Insider reports, from a D-Wave press release, that the Advantage2 system, which has more than 4,400 qubits, has arrived at Villa Saporiti in Como, funded by Swiss Quantum Technology under a 10 million euro agreement, and will be reachable through D-Wave's Leap cloud service once running. Swiss Quantum Technology has bought half of the system's capacity for five years, with an option to buy all of it, and a formal inauguration is planned for 16 Oct 2026.
notes: Data Center Dynamics blocked (403); read The Quantum Insider, which republishes D-Wave press release. Italy first claim is D-Wave and Q-Alliance wording.
